item.title: Marilyn Manson Draws 205,000 Fans to Controversial Free Concert in Mexico
item.description: On August 10, Marilyn Manson drew an estimated 205,000 people to the Teatro del Pueblo at the National Fair of San Luis Potosí (FENAPO) in central Mexico. The free concert, organized by the state government, sparked protests from religious and conservative groups who said the artist was “inappropriate” for what they considered a family-oriented event.

item.title: Disturbed's DAVID DRAIMAN On Crowd Reaction At Sabbath Farewell: 'A Few Jew Hating Morons'
item.description: Disturbed frontman David Draiman took the stage at Black Sabbath’s Back to the Beginning farewell event on July 5, held at Villa Park in Birmingham. What should have been a tribute moment turned into a noisy reception for the singer, who was booed by parts of the crowd before performing “Shot in the Dark” and “Sweet Leaf” as part of a rotating supergroup lineup.

item.title: DISTURBED's DAVID DRAIMAN Booed by Some Fans at BLACK SABBATH's Final Show; VIDEO
item.description: Disturbed’s frontman David Draiman stepped onto the stage at Back to the Beginning, the all-star farewell concert for Ozzy Osbourne and Black Sabbath, and was met with a crowd that didn’t quite know how to respond (watch below).

item.title: U.S. Bans British Punk Duo BOB VYLAN After GLASTONBURY Protest Chants: 'We’re Not The Problem, We’re The Symptom'
item.description: The U.S. State Department has revoked the visas of British rap-punk group Bob Vylan following a controversial performance at the Glastonbury Festival. The move comes after the band’s frontman led the crowd in political chants that included strong criticism of Israel’s military.

item.title: GLASTONBURY FESTIVAL Condemns BOB VYLAN Performance: 'We are appalled by the statements made', Police Investigating
item.description: Glastonbury Festival organizers have issued a public statement criticizing punk duo Bob Vylan after their controversial set on Saturday. The performance included political messages, a chant targeting the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF), and comments that festival leaders say went too far.

item.title: IRON MAIDEN Fans Slam 50th Anniversary Tour: 'Most Predictable Setlist Possible'
item.description: Iron Maiden launched their Run for Your Lives 50th anniversary tour on May 27 in Budapest, Hungary. Grab Your Tickets Here. The show introduced Simon Dawson behind the drums, stepping in after Nicko McBrain retired in late 2024.

item.title: Jethro Tull’s Ian Anderson Slams Brazilian Fans & iPhones: "Crowds Are Worse Than Ever"
item.description: So Ian Anderson, flute-wielding sorcerer of JETHRO TULL, has had it with you people—yes, YOU, the one recording an entire concert through a cracked iPhone 8 with 2% battery while also screaming “PLAY THICK AS A BRICK!

item.title: Slipknot's New 'S' Logo Sparks Outrage Among Fans
item.description: Slipknot has rolled out a batch of limited edition merchandise, and one particular shirt seems to have set off quite the tempest. On the front? The band’s name—classic enough.

item.title: Jaime Bennington, Chester Bennington's Son Calls Out Linkin Park
item.description: Linkin Park thought they were shaking things up by naming Emily Armstrong their new vocalist, but it’s more like they kicked a hornet’s nest while blindfolded. Fans aren’t just upset—they’re seething.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING's Tim Lambesis on New Album: “As Passionate as Ever”
item.description: Tim Lambesis, the ever-controversial voice behind AS I LAY DYING, let slip in a recent chat with the Today’s Boondoggle podcast that the band’s next studio album is set to land later this year (2024).
